空港からホテル、観光地まで。佐藤さんと一緒に、初めての中国でも困らない「使えるひ: From the airport to your hotel and the sights. Learn the handy phrases that will get you through your first trip to China, together with Sato.
金曜の夜九時、上海・浦東空港から地下鉄を乗り継いで、佐藤さんはようやく南京路近く: Nine o'clock on a Friday night. After changing subway lines on the way from Shanghai's Pudong Airport, Sato has finally reached his hotel near Nanjing Road. His first time in China, his first solo trip. As he wheels his suitcase toward the front desk, a smiling staff member, Li Na, greets him.
ホテルのフロント係。二十代後半、テキパキしていて英語も少し話せる: Front desk clerk at the hotel. Late twenties, efficient, and speaks a little English
東京の会社員、二十八歳。休暇で初めて上海へ。中国語は勉強して半年: Office worker from Tokyo, 28. In Shanghai for the first time on vacation. Has been studying Chinese for six months
ホテルのスタッフとお客さん。スタッフは「您」を使って丁寧に話すが、日本ほどかしこ: A hotel staff member and a guest. The staff member speaks politely using 「您」, but without the elaborate honorifics you might expect. For the guest, 「你好」 and 「谢谢」 are enough, and there's no need to be humble. Short, clear and with a smile works best.
こんばんは、いらっしゃいませ。ご予約はございますか。: Good evening! Welcome. Do you have a reservation?
「您」は「你」の丁寧形で、お店やホテルのスタッフがお客さんによく使います。「欢迎: 「您」 is the polite form of 「你」, often used by shop and hotel staff with customers. 「欢迎光临」 is the set phrase for "Welcome." You don't need to reply; it's fine to get straight to the point.
こんばんは、予約しています。佐藤健太です。: Hello, I have a reservation. My name is Kenta Sato.
日本人の名前は中国語読みされます。佐藤健太は「Zuǒténg Jiàntài」。: Japanese names are read the Chinese way. 「佐藤健太」 is 「Zuǒténg Jiàntài」. Even if the clerk doesn't catch it, don't panic; showing your booking screen or passport gets it across instantly.
かしこまりました。パスポートを拝見できますか。: OK, may I see your passport, please?
中国のホテルでは外国人の宿泊登録にパスポートが必須です。「出示」は「提示する」と: At Chinese hotels, a passport is required to register foreign guests. 「出示」 is a slightly formal word meaning "to present." Adding 「一下」 softens it to "please just...."
物を手渡すときは「给你」（丁寧にするなら「给您」）。日本の感覚で「すみません」と: When handing something over, say 「给你」 (or 「给您」 to be polite). If you say "sorry" as you hand it over, the other person may be puzzled for a moment about what you're apologizing for.
佐藤様、ダブルルームを三泊でご予約ですね。: Mr. Sato, you've booked a double room for three nights, is that right?
「先生」は男性への敬称で「〜さん／〜様」。先生（教師）の意味ではありません。女性: 「先生」 is a title for men, "Mr."; it doesn't mean "teacher." For women it's 「女士」 ("Ms."). 「大床房」 is a double room, and 「双床房」 a twin room.
チェックインの際にデポジット五百元が必要です。WeChat Pay とアリペイ、: Check-in requires a 500-yuan deposit. Will you use WeChat or Alipay?
「押金」はデポジット（預かり金）。チェックアウト時に返金されます。「块」は「元」: 「押金」 is a deposit, refunded when you check out. 「块」 is the spoken word for 「元」, and when stating prices people almost always say 「块」. These days you can register foreign credit cards with Alipay and WeChat Pay too.
はい、このコードを読み取っていただければ大丈夫です。……完了しました。こちらがカ: Yes, just scan this code. ...All done. Here's your key card. Your room is on the twelfth floor.
「十」shí と「四」sì は日本人がよく聞き間違える組み合わせ。部屋番号や階数: 「十」 (「shí」) and 「四」 (「sì」) are a pair learners often mishear. For room numbers and floors, it's reassuring to show the number on your fingers or ask them to show you a note, just in case.
ありがとう。ちなみに、朝食は何時からですか。: Thank you. By the way, what time does breakfast start?
朝六時半から十時まで、二階のレストランです。: From 6:30 to 10 in the morning, in the restaurant on the second floor.
パスワードや電話番号、部屋番号など「数字で答えるもの」は「是多少？」で聞きます。: Things answered with numbers, like passwords, phone numbers and room numbers, are asked about with 「是多少？」. 「是什么？」 also works, but 「多少」 is much more natural.
パスワードはカードキーのケースに書いてあります。何かあればいつでもフロントにお電: The password is written on the key card holder. If you have any problems, call the front desk anytime.
「太〜了」は気持ちが大きいときの「すごく〜」。疲れていても最後にこのひと言を笑顔: 「太……了」 means "so...," for strong feelings. If you can say this with a smile at the end, even when you're tired, the staff will naturally respond more warmly.
ホテル・レストラン・チケットに使う。「我有预订」＝予約しています。「预约」は病院: Used for hotels, restaurants and tickets. 「我有预订」 = I have a reservation. 「预约」 is more for appointments at hospitals, government offices and so on
ホテル、高速鉄道、観光地のチケット購入でもよく求められる。旅行中はすぐ出せる場所: Often required at hotels, for high-speed rail and when buying tickets for tourist sites. Keep it somewhere handy while traveling
「办理入住」＝チェックイン手続きをする。ホテルの案内表示でもよく見る: 「办理入住」 = to go through check-in. Often seen on hotel signs
「几点退房？」＝チェックアウトは何時？ 延長は「晚点退房」: 「几点退房？」 = What time is checkout? Late checkout is 「晚点退房」
ホテル・レンタル・シェア自転車でも登場。「退押金」＝デポジットを返す: Also comes up at hotels, rentals and shared bikes. 「退押金」 = to refund a deposit
「房卡丢了」＝カードキーをなくした。エレベーターにかざさないと動かないホテルも多: 「房卡丢了」 = I lost my key card. At many hotels the elevator won't move unless you tap it
ツインは「双床房」。予約サイトでも同じ表記なので覚えておくと便利: A twin room is 「双床房」. Booking sites use the same terms, so they're handy to know
「打前台电话」＝フロントに電話する。部屋の電話の「0」や「9」が直通のことが多い: 「打前台电话」 = to call the front desk. Often "0" or "9" on the room phone goes straight through
「含早餐吗？」＝朝食付きですか。中国のホテルの朝食は粥や包子が並ぶのが楽しみ: 「含早餐吗？」 = Is breakfast included? Chinese hotel breakfasts with congee and steamed buns are something to look forward to
Wi-Fi、スマホ決済、金庫など何でも「密码」。聞くときは「密码是多少？」: Wi-Fi, mobile payments, safes: everything has a 「密码」. To ask, say 「密码是多少？」
「十二楼」＝十二階。「层」も階だが、会話では「楼」がよく使われる: 「十二楼」 = the twelfth floor. 「层」 also means floor, but 「楼」 is common in conversation
「扫一下」＝ちょっと読み取って。中国生活でいちばん使う動詞と言ってもいい: 「扫一下」 = scan it. You could call it the verb you'll use most in daily life in China
「微信」（WeChat Pay）と並ぶ二大スマホ決済。「用支付宝付」＝アリペイで: One of the two big mobile payment systems, along with 「微信」 (WeChat Pay). 「用支付宝付」 = to pay with Alipay
知らない人に質問するときの最初のひと言。日本語の「すみません、ちょっとお聞きした: The first words when asking a stranger a question. It's like "Excuse me, could I ask...?" In China, starting with 「请问」 gets your point across more smoothly than opening with an apology, and the other person gets ready to listen.
すみません、トイレはどこですか。: Excuse me, where is the restroom?
すみません、ここはカードで払えますか。: Excuse me, can I pay by card here?
すみません、地下鉄の駅へはどう行けばいいですか。: Excuse me, how do I get to the subway station?
A + 还是 + B ？（文末に「吗」はつけない）: A + 还是 + B ? (don't put 「吗」 at the end)
二択で相手に選んでもらう聞き方。日本人がよくやってしまうのが「你喝茶还是咖啡吗？: A way of asking someone to choose between two options. A common mistake is adding 「吗」, as in 「你喝茶还是咖啡吗？」. 「还是」 itself makes the question, so 「吗」 isn't needed. When answering, just say the one you choose.
WeChat Pay とアリペイ、どちらにしますか。: Will you use WeChat or Alipay?
お茶にする？ それともコーヒー？: Do you want tea or coffee?
地下鉄で行く？ それともタクシー？: Shall we take the subway or a taxi?
……すればOK、……で十分: just... and you're done; ... is enough
「それだけで大丈夫ですよ」と相手を安心させる言い方。お店やホテルのスタッフがよく: A way of reassuring someone: "That's all it takes." Shop and hotel staff use it a lot. When you say it yourself, it's a very handy expression for modest or simple requests too, as in 「我要一个就行」 ("One is enough").
ホテル、空港のカウンター、観光案内所など、スタッフに用件を伝える場面全般。「你好: All kinds of situations where you tell staff what you need: hotels, airport counters, tourist information centers. With the three-part set of 「你好」, what you need, then 「谢谢」, most exchanges go smoothly.
日本人は「すみません」を連発しがちですが、中国語の「对不起」「不好意思」を何度も: You may be in the habit of saying "sorry" a lot, but if you keep saying 「对不起」 or 「不好意思」 in Chinese, people will think you've done something wrong. When you're thanking someone, saying 「谢谢」 instead of apologizing lets the other person respond happily.
フロントのスタッフは一日に何十人も対応しています。片言でも中国語で「你好」と話し: Front desk staff deal with dozens of guests a day. When a foreigner speaks to them in Chinese, even broken Chinese, with a 「你好」, they're often a little pleased and explain things slowly and carefully.
初めて中国のホテルに泊まると、スタッフの対応が日本よりあっさりしていて「冷たいの: The first time you stay at a Chinese hotel, the staff may seem more matter-of-fact than you're used to, and you might wonder if they're being cold. But it's also a practical kind of kindness: they want guests who arrive late at night to get to rest quickly. In fact, if you ask for "some hot water" or "extra towels," they'll usually bring them right away. The important thing is not to hold back too much, to ask clearly, and to finish with a smile and 「谢谢」. If you say something wrong, just say it again. That first brave sentence will make your trip much more fun.
フロントで「请出示一下您的护照」と言われました。何を求められていますか。: At the front desk, you're told 「请出示一下您的护照」. What are you being asked to do?
「出示」は提示する、「护照」はパスポート。中国のホテルでは外国人の宿泊登録にパス: 「出示」 means to present, and 「护照」 means passport. At Chinese hotels, a passport is required to register foreign guests.
Wi-Fi のパスワードを聞くとき、いちばん自然なのは？: What's the most natural way to ask for the Wi-Fi password?
数字で答えるものは「是多少？」で聞くのが自然。「几个」は個数、「怎么样」は様子を: It's natural to ask about things answered with numbers using 「是多少？」. 「几个」 asks how many items, and 「怎么样」 asks how something is.
「您用微信还是支付宝？」に対する答えとして正しいのは？: Which is a correct answer to 「您用微信还是支付宝？」?
「还是」の質問には選んだ方だけを答えます。「是的」では答えになっていません。: For a 「还是」 question, just answer with the one you choose. 「是的」 doesn't answer the question.
スタッフに親切にしてもらったとき、中国でいちばん気持ちが伝わるのは？: When staff have been kind to you, what gets your feelings across best in China?
日本的に謝るより、感謝をストレートに伝える方が相手も嬉しいもの。「没关系」は「気: Rather than apologizing, people are happier when you thank them directly. 「没关系」 means "never mind," a line for the person being apologized to.
